findings.title: Un-delta'd 'Final assessment phrasings depend on mode' contradicts the run-and-paste contract
findings.recommendation: The baseline mandates skill-authored stock final-assessment phrasings (gate verdicts + eligibility lines + convergence buckets), and its as-of-completion scenario (:167-174) hard-codes render-before-persist with a synthetic-pass computation — the delta inverts the order (persist first, then --report) and PROHIBITS hand-rendering exactly那 tail. Post-apply the baseline would require and prohibit an AI-authored gate line simultaneously, and mandate synthetic-pass machinery the persist-first ordering moots. Add a MODIFIED delta re-scoping the final assessment to the engine-rendered tail; the convergence-bucket routing moves into the engine's canonical-next computation or is explicitly retired with reasons preserved as gate-reason strings.

findings.title: Un-delta'd conventions 'Final-assessment phrasings' reporting standard
findings.recommendation: Conventions mandates stock 'All checks passed. Ready <gate>.' lines for review reports; under D4 the review report ends in the engine tail — no skill-authored stock line exists. The requirement cannot be deleted (audit-drift uses it): add a MODIFIED delta scoping it to audit-drift/architecture-mode reports and pointing review reports at orbit-report-rendering.

findings.title: Un-delta'd 'Walk-mode by default with --batch opt-in' contradicts the three-lane protocol
findings.recommendation: Its Walk-mode UX paragraph (:343) mandates a per-finding AskUserQuestion the obvious-fix lane abolishes and the decision lane demotes; its Batch-mode UX (:345) + 'Batch-mode preserves decision-fork prompts' scenario (:374-377) mandate the fork prompt STILL fires — contradicting prompt-as-optional-closure and chat ratification. Add a FOURTH MODIFIED block: walk-mode UX → lane-per-finding cycle without mandatory prompts; batch-mode UX → per-finding briefing and ratification per the delta's own batch-lifecycle scenario.

findings.title: Un-delta'd 'Resolution-log JSON shape extensions' breaks the delta's own cross-reference
findings.recommendation: (a) The delta records ratified_via 'per Resolution-log JSON shape extensions' but no delta adds the field there — dangling citation. (b) The baseline shape still lists discuss_invoked and two [discuss] scenarios the delta retires. (c) chosen 'matches one of options_presented[].label' fails for off-menu chat directives. Add a MODIFIED block: drop discuss_invoked + the [discuss] scenarios, add ratified_via and a named field for the recorded batch-delegation directive, and define chosen semantics for chat-ratified/off-menu resolutions.

findings.title: External render unimplementable from the cited parsed form; strict validation as written rejects every external pass
findings.recommendation: TrailPass carries only {title, file} per finding — :line STRIPPED (trail.ts:66-68), no Description, no reviewer/date/Notes — yet the grammar requires title, file:line, recommendation VERBATIM and the external scenario requires reviewer+date from the parsed header; nothing tasks extending the parser. Separately the strict-validation field set (spine + mode + scorecard + findings shape) has no genre split, so a literal implementation rejects every external — contradicting one-grammar. Add a task extending the external parse (description→recommendation, line retained, reviewer/date, Notes disposition) into the normalized render shape, and split the validation field set per genre (internal: full; external: confident parse = valid, scorecard/commentary sections defined omitted or Notes-mapped).

findings.title: The no-orientation-delta claim fails on one clause
findings.recommendation: The bare-status requirement asserts 'all --change behavior [is] byte-identical to pre-capability output' — --report is NEW --change behavior (pre-capability it errored on the unknown flag).

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Add a one-line MODIFIED orientation delta scoping the byte-identical clause to the pre-existing --change surface

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Record the historical-claim reading explicitly in design.md so audit-drift's staleness checks don't trip on it (no delta)

findings.title: Lane-preview timing conflicts with per-finding classify ordering
findings.recommendation: The triage preview needs ALL findings lane-classified before any fix, but the retained scenarios keep classification after pushback INSIDE each finding's sequential walk cycle. Specify: triage performs a provisional classification for the preview; walk-time pushback may reclassify, and a reclassified item is announced before its fix.

findings.title: 'Fence-aware external-markdown parse' is factually false
findings.recommendation: parseExternalMarkdown (trail.ts:196-244) does no fence tracking — a code fence containing '## CRITICAL'/'### Title' lines would be miscounted (the historical fence-aware fix was requirement-blocks.ts, a different parser).

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Add fence-awareness to the external parser as a task (recommended — the renderer will quote Description bodies that plausibly contain code fences)

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Drop the adjective from the delta and design (accept the miscount edge as pre-existing behavior)

findings.title: Determinism gaps the change's own thesis doesn't tolerate
findings.recommendation: (a) The first-run scenario keeps the baseline's 'omits the note, OR notes First …-mode run' disjunction — a byte-identical renderer must pick one. (b) 'never from any field of the rendered record' vs the trend needing the current pass's counts (post-persist the record IS in the trail) — state whether the trend's last point is the rendered pass. (c) Historical --report <TS>: iteration/trend as-of-that-pass or as-of-now unpinned. (d) 'the shared tie-break' never named; trail.ts:126 sorts by token only (readdir order on ties) — name the rule and task its implementation.

findings.title: --report with zero review passes unspecified
findings.recommendation: A change with no renderable pass (the common pre-review state) has no defined behavior. Specify a clean error naming the empty trail/renderable set, exit non-zero (consistent with strict/loud); add to task 2.2's test list.

findings.title: One baseline scenario and one contract paragraph dropped from the rewritten fork block
findings.recommendation: Baseline 'Single-recommendation finding does NOT surface fork' (:410-413) and the 'Capture in resolution log' paragraph (:394-398, incl. the omit-or-detected:false rule) do not survive the rewrite — the C2 silent-drop class (fingerprints verify the base, not the drop).

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Re-add a non-disjunctive decision-lane scenario carrying the log-omission clause into the rewritten block

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Record the drop as deliberate in design.md with the replacement contract named

findings.title: No Purpose plan for archive
findings.recommendation: The new orbit-report-rendering baseline needs a Purpose at sync; orbit-address-reviews' Purpose ('pushback → classify → fix…') and the generated skill description literal (address-reviews.ts:514) go stale under lane vocabulary. Add the archive-time Purpose/description notes to 5.4 (the D2 precedent) and fold the description-literal refresh into 3.2.

findings.title: Renderer-computed iteration note mandated for a mode with no renderer
findings.recommendation: The MODIFIED requirement mandates the note be renderer-computed with no architecture-mode carve-out, yet the render surface is --change-only and the ADDED requirement leaves architecture hand-rendering. Scope the mandate to proposal/system; architecture explicitly on the interim hand-computed path.

findings.title: Reference-doc ripple not tasked
findings.recommendation: run-summary-schema.md's stale_suppressed note says suppressions 'don't appear in the user-facing report' — the render grammar makes them a first-class section. Task 3.4 already edits the file; extend it to correct the note.

findings.title: Two small surface edges
findings.recommendation: (a) --report combined with --json: specify clean-error vs ignore. (b) An explicit <TS> matching both an internal emit and an external file: the tie-break is stated only for newest-selection.

findings.title: Naming and scoping polish
findings.recommendation: The requirement name no longer describes its rewritten content (kept to avoid RENAMED — add the one-line design note so a future rename isn't re-litigated); the greppable hand-rendering prohibition needs wording visibly exempting architecture mode so the 5.2 grep and the interim hand-render can't be read as conflicting.

findings.title: Exit-criterion-2 grep is a weaker proxy than the arc letter
findings.recommendation: The arc says the prompt cannot precede the discussion's CONCLUSION; task 5.2 greps prompt-never-precedes-BRIEFING. Make the greppable body sentence and the 5.2 grep match the arc phrasing (prompt fires only after the discussion concludes without a crisp directive).

stale_suppressed.title: Pushback-suppression scenario vs the grammar's suppressed section
stale_suppressed.evidence: Not a new contradiction — the current hand-rendered format already includes the suppressed section (review.ts:554); the baseline letter has always coexisted with it.

stale_suppressed.title: Chat ratification vs orbit-lifecycle-consent
stale_suppressed.evidence: Verified absent: every consent SHALL scopes to consent-marked schema gates (apply/archive seams); finding resolution is not a lifecycle transition, and the provenance rule's prose-request clause actively supports chat as the strongest signal.

stale_suppressed.title: commentary vs the universal spine; review-external contract; audit-drift phrasings; the zoom-in-door claim
stale_suppressed.evidence: All verified conformant: extensions are open per-command; the external template is upstream of the ingest boundary; audit-drift is outside the renderable genre set with its own phrasing requirement intact; the door is conceptual (bare/--full output regression-pinned unchanged).

commentary: First pass on this change, and the findings form one pattern: the deltas modified the requirements they touched but not the REQUIREMENTS THAT DESCRIBE the machinery being replaced — the final-assessment phrasings (twice, in two capabilities), the walk-mode UX paragraph, the resolution-log shape. That is the same unswept-adjacent-layer genre as D3's template residue, one level up. The fifth CRITICAL is different in kind and the most substantive: the external-render path cites a parsed form that factually cannot supply what the grammar requires — the design was written against an idealized TrailPass. The determinism WARNINGs (the retained or-disjunction, the unnamed tie-break, the as-of-when ambiguity) are the change being held to its own thesis. All five MODIFIED blocks otherwise diffed baseline-verbatim; the consent-model and spine checks came back clean, which removes the two scariest cross-capability risks.
final_assessment: 5 critical issues — three un-delta'd baseline contradictions (final-assessment phrasings in orbit-review AND orbit-conventions; the walk-mode UX requirement), the resolution-log shape breaking the delta's own ratified_via citation, and the unimplementable external-render path — plus 7 warnings and 4 suggestions. The proposal's core decisions are sound; the deltas need to finish claiming the baseline text that describes what they replace.
